articles.title: Telangana IT minister Sridhar Babu on GCCs, Hyderabad's tech vision and ISM at Rising Bharat Summit | Full... - Moneycontrol.com
articles.full_text:
At the Rising Bharat Summit 2026, Duddilla Sridhar Babu, Telangana's Minister for Information Technology, Electronics & Communications, Industries & Commerce, and Legislative Affairs, spoke to Nalin Mehta, Managing Editor, Moneycontrol, on Telangana's push to emerge as a semiconductor manufacturing hub and the support it expects from the Centre. Babu alleged that the state faces "step-motherly treatment" in the allocation of semiconductor incentives under the India Semiconductor Mission, while outlining Telangana's strategy to attract investments beyond Hyderabad into tier-2 and tier-3 cities. He also discussed the state's vision for global capability centres, industrial growth, and India's broader economic ambitions.
Here's the transcript of their conversation at the Rising Bharat Summit 2026:
Nalin Mehta: Thanks very much, Chandra and Mr. Babu. Thanks very much for joining us at Rising Bharat's regional edition in Bengaluru. Chandra, of course, began by talking about Bengaluru as an innovation hub, and she said that Hyderabad would have something to say about that.
Well, you are the right man to respond on behalf of Hyderabad. So let me begin by asking you, sir, if you compare, say, Bengaluru and Hyderabad. Now, Bengaluru remains the leader in terms of the absolute number of GCCs because of its lineage and legacy. But in the last couple of years, the highest number of new GCCs have been commissioned in Hyderabad—over 80, if I am not wrong. So, if you can tell us, Hyderabad is getting more GCCs than any other city.
Has this transformation been by design, and what is your vision for Hyderabad for the next five years?
Duddilla Sridhar Babu: Thank you, Mr. Mehta. In fact, it is a great pleasure to be here in Bengaluru. That too, in a South Indian state, my colleagues are all over here, and I would like to thank Moneycontrol and News18 for bringing everybody onto one platform.
I can see a lot of investor friends over here, a lot of stakeholders over here, who are very keen to know about Hyderabad and the state of Telangana. In fact, when you mentioned how and why, of late, many Global Capability Centres have centred around Hyderabad, I would like to mention that it has not been done in a decade's time. Over a period of two to three decades, the trust and faith that we created among companies abroad, and as you rightly said, the legacy of Karnataka, especially Bengaluru, has always led from the front.
And we see Karnataka, especially Bengaluru, as our healthy competitor. We take the nuances, the best experiences, and the best practices that we can imbibe from Karnataka, especially Bengaluru. Over a period of time, we have been able to raise ourselves to the next level.
For example, when we talk about infrastructure, resources, innovation, and government planning, these are the three or four key areas that we take very seriously and work on to move forward. But every state has enough resources at its disposal. Every state can provide land, every state can provide power, and every state can provide incentives or subsidies because we are all in the rat race.
Nalin Mehta: You were saying when we were coming outside that investors are like people walking through a shopping mall, comparing different states. So, what are the discounts that you offer to investors?
Duddilla Sridhar Babu: Absolutely, absolutely. With due respect to investors coming to different states, they would like to see what is best for them. Like when we go to a shopping mall, we try to select the best quality shirt at the most reasonable price, and one that also looks fashionable.
All these things take shape in the customer's mind while shopping, right? We walk across so many shops in the mall and ultimately end up buying from one shop, depending upon our priorities and necessities.
That's what happens. Most investors go to different states and see the advantages they can get. For example, if they find the required talent available there.
If they find land readily available, and if they see that the city or state has the proper infrastructure—whether physical or digital—that they need for their sector or company, they weigh all these factors and ultimately arrive at a decision on where to set up their operations. That is what we focus on. Over the past two to three years, we have placed strong emphasis on talent creation. We have focused on how the available talent can be curated for the global market, whether through reskilling or upskilling.
Nalin Mehta: So, what is the competitive advantage that Hyderabad brings for investors compared to, say, Bengaluru or Chennai, or Telangana versus Maharashtra or Karnataka? And you're not just competing with them; you're also competing with Vietnam and other countries globally. So, what is it that you tell investors? What is the extra edge that Hyderabad provides, or what is your pitch to investors?
Duddilla Sridhar Babu: Yes, absolutely. It's not just about Bengaluru, Mumbai, Pune, or Noida. We are equally competing with other countries where technology is leading the way. So, why should somebody choose Telangana or Hyderabad? We have the best infrastructure.
If you see the seed that we laid exactly 20 years back with a two-billion-dollar investment in a highly capital-intensive project like the Outer Ring Road, we faced a lot of criticism. I was in the government too, and we faced so much criticism.
People asked why a two-billion-dollar investment was being made in the Outer Ring Road, saying it wouldn't fetch that kind of return. But today, if you see the results and the dividends of that physical infrastructure, the Outer Ring Road can connect every part of Hyderabad within 40 to 50 minutes. It is a remarkable facility.
And then there is the first-ever privately built airport on the PPP model. On an international scale, the airport, the ORR, and the creation of HITEC City have made us much stronger over these last 20 years. And we have not stopped there.
Not only have we created physical infrastructure, but we have also built digital infrastructure. Today, optical fibre connectivity reaches the remotest villages in Telangana. Any company can set up an office there. For example, I hail from a very remote area.
They can even establish a software company there.
Nalin Mehta: You are a five-time MLA from Manthani.
Duddilla Sridhar Babu: Yes, I am. With the blessings of my people from Manthani, I have been able to achieve this.
The optical fibre cable is being laid to the last mile. So you, Mr. Mehta, can set up a company there where networking is not a problem at all.
And I also see that the talent is available. So, this is the main reason. At the same time, we have put in place both physical and digital infrastructure.
We also have talent that meets today's requirements, especially in cutting-edge technologies such as AI, cybersecurity, and data analytics. The required skills are available here. And if you see, it is not just core engineering disciplines. GCCs from around 10 to 11 industry verticals have come here.
Nalin Mehta: So, which are the main industries investing in Hyderabad in terms of GCCs, and which sectors are attracting the most investment?
Duddilla Sridhar Babu: Apart from that, I'd like to mention, despite the technical difficulty, that 46% [Technical Difficulty], and out of that, 26% of the GCCs are from the core software industry. A few are from aerospace, a few from defence, a few from the hospitality industry, and a few from the pharma industry, which already has a strong presence.
One more addition, which no other state has, is the beauty tech industry. For the first time, companies like L'Oréal, the multinational beauty tech leader, have established their GCC here.
So, you see, it's not only about talent or innovation. It's a fusion. We bring together technology and expertise.
When technical expertise combines with core industrial expertise, you see sectors like financial services emerging. Banking and core financial insurance sectors have also come here.
Nalin Mehta: Is BFSI growing in Hyderabad?
Duddilla Sridhar Babu: Yes, the BFSI sector is growing at a rapid pace. These are all the sectors that we showcase. When any company comes to us, we tell them these are the areas of expertise we have and how we are creating and strengthening them.
Nalin Mehta: How long do companies take to get clearance in Hyderabad?
Duddilla Sridhar Babu: Ease of doing business is one area where we rank among the best compared to other states. Within 21 days, we provide all the permissions and licences required for any industry, not just GCCs. And if the required clearance is not granted within the stipulated period, it is treated as a deemed clearance under our ease of doing business policy.
This is something we have consistently worked on, and NITI Aayog has recognised us many times as one of the frontrunners in making business processes easier.
Nalin Mehta: One of the things we hear from companies is that, besides tangible factors, they also look at intangible aspects. They consider things like nightlife, law and order, and how safe the city is for women, especially since they bring in an international workforce.
So, first, is that something you hear from companies? And second, this very unfortunate incident involving the assault of a young woman a couple of days ago in Hyderabad—how does that impact sentiment, and what will you do to address such incidents?
Duddilla Sridhar Babu: Absolutely, you're right. Many companies and employees coming from across the globe look at these aspects first. They look at security in terms of law and order. The second thing is the quality of life. Thirdly, they look at how they are placed in an environment of social tranquillity.
In terms of law and order, we maintain standards where every individual is safeguarded, whether it is their privacy or their personal security. As I rightly mentioned, nearly one million CCTV cameras have been installed across the city. That is one of the measures we have taken. The second is our police force.
Nalin Mehta: In terms of addressing issues when incidents like this happen?
Duddilla Sridhar Babu: Yes. In terms of addressing such incidents, we take stern action and ensure that law and order is maintained in a firm and effective manner.
Thirdly, when it comes to nightlife and other aspects of social life, we are equally supportive. At the same time, we take all necessary measures. For example, our Chief Minister and our government's vision is to make Telangana a drug-free state.
So, keeping all those things in perspective, we will...
Nalin Mehta: Let me ask you a broader question then. We've been focusing on what the state is doing and its competitive advantage.
But there is also another player—the Central Government. You all have to work in tandem with it. So, when you deal with the Central Government on investments and related matters, what challenges do you face? What kind of changes or support are you looking for from the Central Government?
Are you getting the support that you need, or do you want more?
Duddilla Sridhar Babu: You know, in this federal polity, all states require assistance from the Central Government. There are so many schemes and programmes of the Central Government that aim to help all states move forward. That is how Rising Bharat, as you mentioned, takes shape. Sometimes, however, what we literally face is stepmotherly treatment under certain Central Government policies. That is what our people are experiencing.
For example, let me cite the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM). We would like to take advantage of it. Whether it is Karnataka, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, or Puducherry, these are states with strong capabilities.
All these states have the capability to manufacture chips. We are competent enough. Hyderabad hosts all the top five chip design companies. We are basically designing chips here.
When a chip manufacturing proposal comes to us, the application is forwarded to the Central Government for consideration under the ISM. When it is not considered, the apathy of the Central Government ultimately affects the people of Telangana, our software professionals, and our chip designers, who design chips not only for India but also for companies abroad. So, when proposals to establish chip manufacturing units here are not approved under the ISM, it causes great heartburn for us.
We have appealed to the Central Government many times. It must provide positive encouragement to states like Telangana. I would also like to say that states which have the capability to manufacture chips should be encouraged. I am not disputing the selection of any other state, but the Central Government should also support other capable states, help them build capacity, and enable them to compete.
That is how Rising Bharat and the vision for 2047 can be achieved. It will happen only if the Central Government acts in a fair and equitable manner. Otherwise, you cannot build Rising Bharat.
Nalin Mehta: Ladies and gentlemen, Mr. Babu has also been a top-class cricketer. He has played for Nizam College and the University of Hyderabad. He is clearly batting on the front foot on the Central Government issue as well.
So, sir, when you have an issue with the Central Government, do you take it up with them? What response do you receive when you raise these concerns?
Duddilla Sridhar Babu: Yes, many times we take up these issues with our senior colleagues in the Union Government. They assure us that next time they will try to do whatever best they can.
We always live in hope. Hopefully, under ISM 2.0, we will get our due share. That is my hope. We will continue to convince the Central Government. They need to understand the genuine concerns of a capable IT state like Telangana and the potential of our people and employees. That understanding is very important.
Time and again, we will continue to press our case, present our arguments, and provide all the necessary facts before them so that chip manufacturing comes to Hyderabad and Telangana.
Nalin Mehta: Last question. We're running out of time. Hyderabad, of course, is a technology hub. You have many greenfield projects coming in, but other cities also have their own strengths. Do you have plans to expand investments beyond Hyderabad and create other hubs across the state?
Duddilla Sridhar Babu: Yes, that's the right question.
Telangana is a very small state, and Hyderabad is its focal point. We are also working towards developing Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. As I mentioned earlier, we have extended digital infrastructure to Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities and even to smaller villages.
That work has already been done, and the talent is available there as well. We are encouraging investors and companies to establish GCCs in these locations and move forward. We are also evolving policies that offer incentives and subsidies to encourage companies to set up operations in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.
One more point I would like to mention is that India has to look ahead. For a long time, we have served as the back office for many multinational corporations. It is like the old saying—you export dough and buy back bread at a higher price.
That is what we have been doing in IT as well. Now technology is taking a new direction, and Hyderabad and the state of Telangana believe that these Global Capability Centres should become Value Centres.
Nalin Mehta: One quick question, sir. With data centres, there are concerns about environmental costs—water consumption, electricity usage, and sustainability. How would you address those concerns, considering Hyderabad is a major growth centre?
Duddilla Sridhar Babu: Yes. Data centres are essential for new technologies, especially AI, because of the processing speed that companies require. As you know, the two biggest resources they consume are water and power.
We are working on this. We have adequate power and sufficient water, and we will provide whatever is required. We are putting all the necessary infrastructure in place to ensure that data centres come to Telangana so that AI-based companies establish themselves in Hyderabad and continue to grow.
